taxonomy:
Here's a taxonomy of grid-based logic games based on the provided rules:

**I. Placement/Coloring Games**

*   **A. Light Placement:**
    *   **Akari:** Place light bulbs (circles) in white squares. Numbers indicate adjacent bulbs. Bulbs illuminate white squares.
*   **B. Cell Coloring/Shading:**
    *   **Dotchi-Loop:** Paint cells black. Black cells form rectangles/squares. White cells do not form rectangles/squares. Numbers indicate area size.
    *   **Evolomino:** Divide grid into blocks. Blocks contain pairs of same-shaped areas (white/gray). Numbers indicate half the block's cell count.
    *   **Five Cells:** Draw squares in white cells. Squares form blocks. Blocks contain one square on an arrow. Arrows pass through at least two blocks.
    *   **Fillomino:** Divide grid into blocks of five cells. Numbers indicate surrounding lines. Lines surround cells, not blocks.
    *   **Hitori:** Color cells. No number appears more than once per row/column. Black cell sides don't touch. White cells form a continuous network.
    *   **Kurodoko:** Color cells black. Numbers indicate white cells to nearest black cell/frame. Numbered cells are white. Black cells don't touch. White cells are connected.
    *   **Kurotto:** Fill (color) cells. Numbers in circles are sums of continuous black cells (vertical/horizontal). Cells with circles cannot be colored.
    *   **LITS:** Color tetrominoes in areas. Same-shaped tetrominoes don't touch (except corners). Colored squares form a connected network. No 2x2 colored squares.
    *   **Nurikabe:** Fill cells. Numbers indicate continuous white cells. White cells are separated by black cells. Black cells form a continuous wall. No 2x2 black cells.
    *   **Nuritwin:** Shade cells. Regions have two blocks of same-sized cells. Numbers indicate block size. Shaded cells are connected. Two blocks in a region don't touch. No 2x2 shaded cells.
    *   **Tilepaint:** Color tiles. Numbers in diagonal cells indicate black cells to the right/down in that line/column. Cells in a tile are all colored or uncolored.
    *   **Usowan:** Fill (color) cells. Numbered cells cannot be colored. Numbers indicate adjacent colored cells (vertical/horizontal). Rooms have one wrong number. Colored cells don't touch. White cells not separated by colored cells.
*   **C. Block Formation/Identification:**
    *   **Chained Block:** Fill cells. Consecutive black cells form blocks. Numbers indicate block size. "?" indicates unknown size. Blocks in contact at corners form chains. Chains have only one block size/shape.
    *   **Choco Banana:** Fill cells. Consecutive black cells form blocks. Numbers indicate block size. "?" indicates unknown size. Blocks in contact at corners form chains. Chains have only one block size/shape.
    *   **Makaro:** Fill cells. Cells with circles are "Misaki" (white). Other white cells are not Misaki. White Misaki cells have one adjacent white cell, others black. Numbers in circles indicate straight white lines from Misaki. White cells form a continuous network. No 2x2 black or white cells.
    *   **Shakashaka:** Place black triangles. Four kinds of triangles. Cannot place in black squares. White areas form rectangles/squares. Numbers indicate adjacent black triangles (vertical/horizontal).

**II. Path/Loop Drawing Games**

*   **A. Single Loop:**
    *   **Dotchi-Loop:** Draw lines through cell centers to make a single loop. Loop goes through white circles. Loop doesn't cross itself, branch, or repeat cells. Loop avoids black circles.
    *   **Masyu:** Make a single loop through cell centers. Loop goes through all white/black circles. White circles: straight through, right-angled turn in adjacent cell. Black circles: right-angled turn, then straight through next cell.
    *   **Nagareru:** Draw a line to make a single continuous loop. Loop goes through cell centers. Loop doesn't cross itself, branch, or repeat cells. Loop goes through arrow cells. Arrows show wind direction. Loop cannot go against wind. Side winds require movement in wind direction.
    *   **Pencils:** Draw lines from pencil tips. Lines go through cells from tip. Pencil length is indicated by numbers. Lines don't cross or branch.
    *   **Slitherlink:** Connect adjacent dots with vertical/horizontal lines to make a single loop. Numbers indicate surrounding lines. Empty cells have any number of lines. Loop doesn't cross or branch.
    *   **Suraromu:** Make a single loop through cell centers. Loop doesn't cross itself, branch, or repeat cells. Dotted lines are "Gates." Loop must pass all Gates once. Loop starts and ends at open numbered circle. Number in circle is number of Gates to pass. Numbers at Gate ends show crossing point.
    *   **Yajilin:** Draw a line to make a single loop. Loop goes through cell centers. Loop doesn't cross itself, branch, or repeat cells. Numbers show black cells in arrow direction. Loop avoids black cells and numbered cells. Black cells don't touch.
*   **B. Multiple Paths/Connections:**
    *   **Hebi:** Place numbers 1-5 in squares to form snakes. Snakes connect sequentially. Snakes don't touch sides. Snake view direction: another snake cannot be in next black square or grid rim. Black squares show nearest number in arrow direction. 0 means no snake in that direction.
    *   **Numberlink:** Connect pairs of same numbers with a continuous line. Lines go through cell centers. Lines don't cross, branch, or go through numbered cells.
    *   **Hashiwokakero:** Connect islands (circles with numbers) with bridges. Number of bridges equals island number. Max two bridges between islands. Bridges don't cross islands or other bridges. Bridges form a continuous link.

**III. Number/Value Placement Games**

*   **A. Number Placement within Constraints:**
    *   **Chained Block:** Fill cells. Consecutive black cells form blocks. Numbers indicate block size. "?" indicates unknown size. Blocks in contact at corners form chains. Chains have only one block size/shape.
    *   **Choco Banana:** Fill cells. Consecutive black cells form blocks. Numbers indicate block size. "?" indicates unknown size. Blocks in contact at corners form chains. Chains have only one block size/shape.
    *   **Double Choco:** Divide grid into blocks. Blocks contain pairs of same-shaped areas (white/gray). Numbers indicate half the block's cell count.
    *   **Fillomino:** Divide grid into blocks of five cells. Numbers indicate surrounding lines. Lines surround cells, not blocks.
    *   **Heyawake:** Fill cells. Rooms (bordered by bold lines) have numbers indicating painted cells. Rooms without numbers have any number of painted cells. White cells don't stretch across >2 rooms straight. Painted cells don't touch. White cells not separated by painted cells.
    *   **Juosan:** Fill cells with "-" or "|". Territories (bold lines) have numbers indicating how many "-" or "|" marks they get. Marks extend horizontally (>3 cells) or vertically (>2 cells).
    *   **Nansuke:** Fill blank cells with numbers from a list. Numbers are up/down or left/right. One cell has one digit.
    *   **Ripple Effect:** Fill cells in Rooms. Rooms contain consecutive numbers from 1. Duplicated numbers in row/column have space between equal to or greater than the number's value.
    *   **Satogaeri:** Move circles (vertically/horizontally) so each country (bold lines) has one circle. Numbers in circles indicate cells to pass through. Circles without numbers move any distance. Circles don't cross tracks or go over other circles.
    *   **Shikaku:** Place black triangles. Four kinds of triangles. Cannot place in black squares. White areas form rectangles/squares. Numbers indicate adjacent black triangles (vertical/horizontal).
    *   **Sto-stone:** Fill colored cells. Rooms (bold lines) have numbers indicating continuous black cells. Rooms without numbers have any number of black cells. Black cells don't touch across bold lines. When stones drop, they fill bottom half without empty cells.
    *   **Sudoku:** Place numbers 1-9 in empty cells. Each row, column, and 3x3 block contains all numbers 1-9.
    *   **Yosenabe:** Move circles to gray areas. Arrows show movement (tip in gray cell). Arrows are straight, don't bend, cross, or go over others. Gray area number equals total of entering circle numbers. Empty gray areas have any sum, but at least one circle must enter.
*   **B. Number-based Area/Block Definition:**
    *   **Evolomino:** Divide grid into blocks. Blocks contain pairs of same-shaped areas (white/gray). Numbers indicate half the block's cell count.
    *   **Fillomino:** Divide grid into blocks of five cells. Numbers indicate surrounding lines. Lines surround cells, not blocks.
    *   **Nuritwin:** Shade cells. Regions have two blocks of same-sized cells. Numbers indicate block size. Shaded cells are connected. Two blocks in a region don't touch. No 2x2 shaded cells.
    *   **Sashigane:** Divide grid into L-shaped blocks (one block wide). Blocks are L-shaped. Open circles form the knee. Arrows point towards the knee. Numbers in open circles indicate block size. Marks (arrows/circles) can be 0, 1, 2, or 3.

**IV. Maze/Pathfinding Games**

*   **A. Maze Creation/Navigation:**
    *   **Nurimeizu:** Paint cells to create a maze from S to G across white cells. Rooms (bold lines) are all painted or all white. White cells not cut off by painted cells. White cells don't form loops. Rooms with S, G, circle, triangle cannot be painted. Circle cells on shortest S-G path. Triangle cells not on shortest S-G path. Black/white cells don't form 2x2 squares.
*   **B. Path through Specific Elements:**
    *   **Mid-loop:** Fill cells with numbers. Rooms (bold lines) contain numbers 1 to cell count. Black cells with arrows: number is max of surrounding cells in arrow direction. Numbers not adjacent to same number in another room.
    *   **Moon-or-Sun:** Draw a single loop. Loop goes through cell centers. Loop doesn't cross, branch, or repeat cells. Rooms (bold lines) are traversed once. Loop goes through all moon cells OR all sun cells in a room, not both. After moons in one room, must go through suns in next room, and vice versa.

**V. Grid Division Games**

    *   **Sto-stone:** Fill colored cells. Rooms (bold lines) have numbers indicating continuous black cells. Rooms without numbers have any number of black cells. Black cells don't touch across bold lines. When stones drop, they fill bottom half without empty cells.
